scenes.text: Deep inside Yellowstone National Park, there is a fifty-square-mile strip of land known as the Zone of Death.
Because of a bizarre constitutional loophole, if you were to commit a crime here, a court might not be able to prosecute you.
The law requires a jury from the state and district where the crime happened, but this uninhabited strip has zero residents.
Would you feel safe camping in this lawless zone, or should they close this loophole immediately?
